research_law: Математика не сходится. Пока не сойдется.
hypothesis: Two different exact certificate languages hidden behind a shared internal Boolean selector can be discovered, composed and used to eliminate that selector without a family/selector oracle.
what_worked: Direct GF2/Hall/Horn recognition was blocked on every guarded original CNF
JANUS discovered a usable selector by enumerating input variables rather than receiving an oracle
Both restrictions were proved UNSAT using different exact languages
The selector was eliminated by a replayable split certificate
Four guarded mixed cases escaped the same 500001-resolvent bounded-DP cap
what_remains_open: How to find a small live interface for arbitrary CNF
Whether arbitrary-CNF interface width is O(log n)
Whether a compressed exact boundary-message language avoids 2^k branch enumeration

post_result_lemma.name: BOOLEAN_BOUNDARY_ENUMERATION_FRONTIER
post_result_lemma.statement: Enumerating all assignments to k Boolean live-boundary variables can require 2^k exact branch certificates. If each branch is polynomial, the composed cost is 2^k poly(n), polynomial when k=O(log n).
post_result_lemma.scope: Resource accounting for the current BCEG branching mechanism; not a lower bound on all possible BCEG message languages.

spiral_connection: This result returns directly to C021/C047: the relevant resource is the amount of exact information crossing the live cut, not merely formula size or the existence of locally small certificates.
